fr:title.text: finite-field-invariants: a reference forest › The symplectic skeleton

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: finite-field-invariants: a reference forest › The symplectic skeleton

fr:mainmatter.html:p: One idea at three scales. Avatar 1 is global, avatar 2 semi-local, avatar 3 infinitesimal; the thesis is that each is the same statement about half an orbit dimension.

The trace form on \mathfrak {gl}_n: \kappa (A, B) = \operatorname {tr}(AB),
perfect over every ring, symmetric, and invariant: \kappa ([P, A], B) = -\kappa (A, [P, B]). Twisted, it identifies \mathfrak {gl}_n with its F-twisted dual.

Restricted to the commutator subspace of a fixed P, its alternation \kappa ([P, A], A) = 0 is the source of every symplectic structure in the program. The Kostant--Kirillov form \omega that makes orbital varieties Lagrangian, the residue form \operatorname {tr}([P, A]B) of (H1), and the survivor cocycle of Wall 1 are all restrictions of it.
Uses: Setup: conjugation over a finite field, The entrywise Frobenius.

Fix \lambda \vdash n with conjugate \lambda '. Then
c(\lambda ) = \sum _{i,j} \min (\lambda _i, \lambda _j) = \sum _j (\lambda '_j)^2, \qquad \dim \mathcal {O}_{\lambda } = n^2 - c(\lambda ), \qquad \dim \mathrm {Fl}_{\lambda '} = \frac {1}{2} \dim \mathcal {O}_{\lambda }.

Mechanism. c(\lambda ) is the dimension of the centralizer of a nilpotent of type \lambda , in every characteristic: the centralizer is the k[T]-module \operatorname {Hom} of the type modules, whose dimension is the stated minimum-sum. For regular \lambda the half is \frac {n(n - 1)}{2} — the height-conjecture dimension, which is why the height conjecture and (*) are the same statement at two scales.
Uses: Setup: conjugation over a finite field.

fr:title.text: The thesis: every bound is half an orbit dimension

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The thesis: every bound is half an orbit dimension

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Every bound the program needs is half of a nilpotent orbit dimension. Nilpotent orbits carry the Kostant--Kirillov form \omega in every characteristic; a subvariety of half dimension inside an orbit sits at the Lagrangian bound, and dimension \le half is exactly what isotropy forces.
The thesis appears at three scales, and the three avatars of the forest are its three instances.

html:ul.html:li: Global — the \omega form on each orbit: orbital varieties are Lagrangian, a theorem.
Semi-local — the residue form \operatorname {tr}([P, A]B) on adjoint torsion at drop points: (H1), a theorem.
Infinitesimal — the survivor cocycle at a pencil germ: (W), a conjecture.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: This is a principle, not a theorem: it is the reason the three avatars have the same shape, and it is what tells you that (*) is the right thing to be stuck on.
Uses: The trace form, The three recurring numbers.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Orbital varieties are Lagrangian
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: distilled.tex sec:kk-lagrangian; journal pass 6--8 apparatus; machine censuses N13--N19 in experiments/pencil_ideal.sage.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Orbital varieties — the irreducible components of \mathcal {O}_{\lambda } \cap \mathfrak {n} for \mathfrak {n} a fixed nilradical, Borel or parabolic — are Lagrangian for the Kostant--Kirillov form \omega on \mathcal {O}_{\lambda }, for every n and every characteristic.

Consequence. The B-stable subvarieties of an orbit that the height program must control sit exactly at half dimension, with the isotropy form available as an identity rather than as a genericity argument. This is avatar 1's mechanism theorem: it supplies the symplectic half of every dimension bound in the program, and it is why the surviving open content of the height conjecture is purely (*).
Uses: The trace form, The three recurring numbers, The thesis: every bound is half an orbit dimension.

fr:title.text: Nilpotent pencils, drop points, the centralizer sheaf

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Nilpotent pencils, drop points, the centralizer sheaf

fr:mainmatter.html:p: A nilpotent pencil is P = \mu N + \nu M, a matrix of linear forms over B = K[\mu , \nu ], every member nilpotent. Its generic Jordan type is \tau , and a drop point is one of the finitely many x \in \mathbb {P}^1 at which the fiber type degenerates.

The commutator map \operatorname {ad}_{P} : \mathfrak {gl}_n \otimes \mathcal {O} \to \mathfrak {gl}_n \otimes \mathcal {O}(1)
on the pencil's \mathbb {P}^1 has kernel the centralizer sheaf \mathcal {C}_{P}. The moving-flag count balances curve freedom against inscribed-pencil freedom through the Riemann--Roch budget \chi (\mathcal {C}_{P}).
Uses: Setup: conjugation over a finite field, The trace form.

fr:title.text: (H1): the incidence theorem for flagless pencils

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (H1): the incidence theorem for flagless pencils
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: distilled.tex Part 3; journal sec:h1; formal/ Lean certificates.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: (H1). Every nilpotent pencil satisfies the incidence bound: the dimension of the space of flags inscribed in the pencil is at most its Riemann--Roch budget \chi (\mathcal {C}_{P}), with equality controlled by the adjoint torsion — for every type and multidegree, every n, every characteristic.

Mechanism. A characteristic-free trace identity. Tangent vectors to constant-type families are commutators over the function field, hence lie in the adjoint torsion, hence are isotropic for the residue form \operatorname {tr}([P, A]B); isotropy becomes a trace identity rather than a genericity argument. The realized subspace is measured Lagrangian (the \delta -law) at every computed drop point.

Consequence. The nilpotent-pencil scheme is unconditionally a complete intersection and the regular-class height bound holds for every n, so the height conjecture rides on the single statement (*). The elementary chain of the proof is formalized in Lean 4 (formal/, no sorry up to the kernel-flatness hypothesis).
Uses: The trace form, Nilpotent pencils, drop points, the centralizer sheaf.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The germ apparatus
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: distilled.tex Part 5; journal passes 8--11 (exponent dictionary, component atlas).

fr:mainmatter.html:p: A pencil germ is a lattice over B = k\lbrack \lbrack u \rbrack \rbrack \lbrack u^{-1} \rbrack , a polynomial-type ring in one variable over the formal power series ring R = k\lbrack \lbrack u \rbrack \rbrack . The survivor algebra of a germ carries a cyclic cocycle; that cocycle is the germ-scale avatar of the trace form.

The exponent dictionary computes its graded pieces: the dimension of the level-m piece is r + \#\{\text {adjoint-torsion exponents of size} \ge m\},
a consequence of the isomorphism \mathcal {C}_{P} \cong \mathcal {O} between the centralizer sheaf of the germ's pencil P and the structure sheaf.

Role in the skeleton. This is avatar 3 — the thesis made infinitesimal. Avatar 2, the residue form \operatorname {tr}([P, A]B), has its u-adic bottom here. Coisotropy of the cocycle is Wall 1; the attempt to upgrade it to a Lagrangian statement is (W).
Uses: The trace form, The thesis: every bound is half an orbit dimension.

fr:title.text: Wall 1: coisotropy of the cyclic cocycle

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Wall 1: coisotropy of the cyclic cocycle
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal pass 6--8 apparatus (Borel/Steinberg, Wall 1); distilled.tex Part 5.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Wall 1. The cyclic cocycle carried by the survivor algebra of a pencil germ is coisotropic.

Role in the skeleton. This is the bottom floor of the avatar tower: the germ-scale instance of the thesis, and the fixed point from which (W) tries to upgrade coisotropy to the full Lagrangian statement. It is a theorem; the upgrade is not.
Uses: The trace form, The germ apparatus.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The anomaly law
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal passes 6--8 (variational identities, thresholds, anomaly law); distilled.tex Part 5.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: (anomaly law). Coisotropy of the survivor cocycle fails only at special characteristic-2 germs.

Role in the skeleton. The law is the bookkeeping for why characteristic 2 is the sole obstruction to characteristic-free statements at germ scale — which germs are anomalous, and why only generic statements survive there.

Status. Open. Measured on the D_4 moment-map probes. Consistent with the small-n record: the one genuine counterexample to a naively-stated survivor identity in the whole program is over \mathbb {F}_q with q = 2 at n = 5.
Uses: Wall 1: coisotropy of the cyclic cocycle, The germ apparatus.

This forest is the canonical statement layer of the finite-field-invariants project: definitions, theorems, conjectures, and the dependency skeleton that links them — kept separate from the narrative journal (notes/steenrod-hsop.tex) and the experiment record (experiments/). Notation is fixed here; when the journal and the forest disagree, the forest wins and the journal gets patched.

Each statement lives at a permanent numeric address. The number means nothing and never changes: nodes are renamed, restated, split and refuted, and the address survives all of it, so a citation written today still resolves after the mathematics moves. The readable concordance is ADDRESSES.md, regenerated by every build.
From the conjugation action to the statement of the height conjecture.

fr:title.text: Setup: conjugation over a finite field

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Setup: conjugation over a finite field

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Fix a prime power q, let k = \mathbb {F}_q and let K = \overline {k}. Let S = k[x_{ij} : 1 \le i, j \le n] be the coordinate ring of \mathrm {M}_n = \mathrm {M}_{n \times n}, with generic matrix X = (x_{ij}), carrying the conjugation action of G = \mathrm {GL}_n(k): the element \sigma \in G maps the variables to the entries of \sigma ^{-1} X \sigma . Write \mathcal {N} \subset \mathrm {M}_n(K) for the nilpotent cone.

The kernel of G \to \mathrm {GL}(\mathrm {M}_n(k)) is the scalars, so the effective group is \widehat {G} \cong \mathrm {PGL}_n(k). For n \ge 2 the order of \widehat {G} is divisible by the characteristic of k, so the action is modular: there is no Reynolds operator, and the classical non-modular invariant theory does not apply.

Role in the skeleton. This node fixes only the ambient objects and the group. The two things the setup produces — the characteristic polynomial coefficients and the entrywise Frobenius — are separate statements, because almost every downstream node rests on one of them and not on the other.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The characteristic polynomial coefficients
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: distilled.tex Part 1; journal sec:setup. The caution was added 2026-08-23, correcting a claim that S^G is generated by the c_{j} — never in the journal, introduced when the node was first written.

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
The characteristic polynomial of the generic matrix X: \chi _{X}(\lambda ) = \lambda ^n - c_{1} \lambda ^{n-1} + c_{2} \lambda ^{n-2} - \cdots + (-1)^n c_{n}, \qquad c_{j} \in S^G, \quad \deg c_{j} = j.
So c_{1} = \operatorname {tr} X and c_{n} = \det X. The signs are irrelevant to everything downstream.
Role in the skeleton. These n invariants are the entire input to the program: the Steenrod ideal is generated by their q-Steenrod powers, and the polarizations are their bihomogeneous parts.

Warning. The c_{j} do not generate S^G. They generate the invariants of the algebraic group \mathrm {GL}_n acting by conjugation; the group here is the finite G = \mathrm {GL}_n(k), and S is integral over S^G, so \dim S^G = n^2 while k[c_{1}, \dots , c_{n}] has dimension n. Already at n = 2, q = 2 the pair (c_{1}, c_{2}) fails to separate conjugacy classes: 0 and \begin {pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \end {pmatrix} agree on both. Only c_{j} \in S^G is used anywhere in the program.
Uses: Setup: conjugation over a finite field.

For M \in \mathrm {M}_n(K), write F(M) for the entrywise Frobenius (m_{ij}) \mapsto (m_{ij}^q). Then F is a bijective ring endomorphism of \mathrm {M}_n(K) which preserves and reflects nilpotency, so F(\mathcal {N}) = \mathcal {N}.

Mechanism. The q-power map is a ring endomorphism of K; its additivity in characteristic p is what makes it compatible with matrix multiplication, and it is bijective because Frobenius is surjective on the algebraically closed K. A bijective ring endomorphism carries nilpotents to nilpotents both ways.

Role in the skeleton. F is the direction in which the whole program deforms. The evaluation identity reads the q-Steenrod operations off the pencil M + T F(M), and the pencil criterion turns membership in V(J) into nilpotency of every member of that pencil. It is also the twist that makes the trace form identify \mathfrak {gl}_n with its F-twisted dual.
Uses: Setup: conjugation over a finite field.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The q-Steenrod operations
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: Maithani 2025; L. Smith, Polynomial Invariants of Finite Groups, Ch.~11.

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
The q-Steenrod operations: the k-algebra homomorphism \mathcal {P} \colon S \to S[T], \qquad x \mapsto x + x^q T
on linear forms, with \mathcal {P}(f) = \sum _{i \ge 0} \mathcal {P}^{i}(f) T^i. Each \mathcal {P}^{i} raises degree by i(q-1) and preserves the invariants of any degree-preserving action. For homogeneous f of degree d with \mathbb {F}_q-coefficients, \mathcal {P}^{i}(f) = 0 \text { for } i > d, \qquad \mathcal {P}^{d}(f) = f^q.
These two vanishing facts are what make the Steenrod ideal finitely generated in the stated degrees.
Uses: Setup: conjugation over a finite field.
For every f \in S and every M \in \mathrm {M}_n(K), \sum _{i \ge 0} \mathcal {P}^{i}(f)(M) T^i = f(M + T F(M)) \qquad \text {in } K[T].

Mechanism. \mathcal {P} is a substitution homomorphism, so it commutes with evaluation. This one line is what the whole height program runs on: Steenrod operations are deformation calculus in the Frobenius direction. Every subsequent statement about V(J) — the pencil criterion, the flag witnesses — is read off it.
Uses: Setup: conjugation over a finite field, The q-Steenrod operations, The entrywise Frobenius.

For commuting indeterminates s, t and two generic matrices X, Y, the polarizations P_{a,b} of c_{j} are defined by c_{j}(sX + tY) = \sum _{a + b = j} s^a t^b P_{a,b}(X, Y),
bihomogeneous of bidegree (a, b), with P_{j,0} = c_{j}(X) and P_{0,j} = c_{j}(Y).

For j \le 4 these are explicit combinations of twisted trace forms \operatorname {tr}(X^{a_1} F(X)^{b_1} \cdots X^{a_r} F(X)^{b_r})
— the sparse trace-form generators. Setting Y = F(X) recovers the q-Steenrod powers, by the evaluation identity.
Uses: The q-Steenrod operations, The evaluation identity, The characteristic polynomial coefficients, The entrywise Frobenius.

J \coloneqq \bigl ( \mathcal {P}^{i}(c_{j}) : 1 \le j \le n, 0 \le i \le j-1 \bigr ) \subseteq S,
an ideal generated by \binom {n+1}{2} = \frac {n(n+1)}{2} invariants, of degrees j + i(q-1).

By the vanishing facts of the q-Steenrod operations the omitted Steenrod powers contribute nothing, so V(J) is the common zero locus of all \mathcal {P}^{i}(c_{j}), i \ge 0. For n = 2 the ideal is exactly Maithani's primary ideal (\operatorname {tr}, \det , \mathcal {P}^{1}(\det )) up to the orbit product.
Uses: The q-Steenrod operations, Polarizations and the trace-form generators, The characteristic polynomial coefficients.

For M \in \mathrm {M}_n(K): M \in V(J) \iff M + t F(M) \text { is nilpotent for every } t \in K.
Equivalently M \in V(J) \iff \operatorname {span}_K \lbrace M, F(M) \rbrace \subseteq \mathcal {N} :
V(J) is the locus of matrices nilpotent to all orders in the Frobenius direction. In particular F(V(J)) = V(J).

Mechanism. Immediate from the evaluation identity: the coefficients of \chi _{M + tF(M)} are the \mathcal {P}^{i}(c_{j})(M), so all of them vanish exactly when every member of the pencil is nilpotent.
Uses: The evaluation identity, The Steenrod ideal.

fr:title.text: Flag witnesses for the partner variety

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Flag witnesses for the partner variety
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal sec:notflag (the n = 3 non-flag component is a cone over a twisted cubic); distilled.tex Part 1.

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
Let \mathfrak {n} be the strictly upper triangular matrices. Then \mathcal {FL} \coloneqq \bigcup _{g \in \mathrm {GL}_n(\mathbb {F}_q)} g \mathfrak {n} g^{-1} \subseteq V(J),
a finite union of linear subspaces of dimension \frac {n(n - 1)}{2}, indexed by the \mathbb {F}_q-rational complete flags.

More generally any nilpotent M with [M, F(M)] = 0 lies in V(J), as does any M such that M and F(M) are strictly triangular with respect to a common flag. For n = 2 these mechanisms exhaust V(J); already for n = 3 they do not, so the flag locus is not all of the partner variety — only, conjecturally, all of it up to dimension.
Uses: The pencil criterion.

fr:title.text: The Krull bound: only the upper bound is open

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The Krull bound: only the upper bound is open

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Consequence. The whole content of the height conjecture is therefore an upper bound on \dim V(J). The generators of J extend to a homogeneous system of parameters if and only if the conjectured height holds.
Uses: The Steenrod ideal, Flag witnesses for the partner variety.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The height conjecture
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: distilled.tex Part 1; journal thm:height-n7, thm:m8, cor:height-n8, cor:height-n9.

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
For every n and every prime power q, \operatorname {ht} J = \frac {n(n+1)}{2}, \qquad \text {equivalently} \qquad \dim V(J) = \frac {n(n - 1)}{2}:
the \frac {n(n+1)}{2} invariants \mathcal {P}^{i}(c_{j}), 0 \le i < j \le n, form a regular sequence in S and extend to a homogeneous system of parameters. The conjectured dimension is \dim \mathrm {Fl} — up to dimension, the flag witnesses must be everything.

Status. Proven for n \le 5 every q (height at n \le 5); for characteristic 0, every n; for all but finitely many characteristics per n, ineffectively; and for n \le 9 every q (height at n \le 9). Open in general, and what is open is exactly (*).
Uses: The Steenrod ideal, The Krull bound: only the upper bound is open.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (*): the characteristic-p subvariety inference
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: distilled.tex Part 3; journal sec:h1 and the pass 6--8 apparatus.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: (*): for every proper B-stable irreducible subvariety W of a nilpotent orbit \mathcal {O}_{\lambda }, the isotropy bound holds — \dim W \le \frac {1}{2} \dim \mathcal {O}_{\lambda }.

Role in the skeleton. After (H1) this is the single remaining geometric statement between the program and the height conjecture. Orbital varieties are Lagrangian supplies it whenever W is an orbital variety; what is left is the case of subvarieties carrying \ge 2 moduli of B-orbits, where characteristic p denies the generic-smoothness argument. First possible at n = 6, which is why the ladder height at n \le 9 has to be climbed by hand.
The infinitesimal form of the same statement is (W).
Uses: Orbital varieties are Lagrangian, (H1): the incidence theorem for flagless pencils.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Height at n ≤ 9
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal thm:height-n7, cor:height-n8, cor:height-n9; commits afdac1f, e8c7430.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The height conjecture holds for every n \le 9 and every prime power q. Unconditionally for n \le 7; for n = 8, 9 conditional on published modality rows and machine certificates.

The ladder is climbed rung by rung, because (*) is unavailable and each n has to be discharged by its own count. The rungs are height at n \le 5, height at n \le 7, height at n = 8 and height at n = 9; their conditionality differs and is stated on each.
Uses: The height conjecture, Height at n ≤ 5, Height at n ≤ 7, Height at n = 8, Height at n = 9.

fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal sec:small-n; Kashiarov, Hille--Röhrle for the finiteness input.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The height conjecture holds for every n \le 5 and every prime power q.

Mechanism. For n \le 5 the Borel has finitely many orbits on the nilradical (Kashiarov; Hille--Röhrle), so (*) is not needed: the isotropy bound of the orbital-variety theorem, plus at most one modulus of orbits, covers every B-stable irreducible subvariety.
Uses: The height conjecture, Orbital varieties are Lagrangian.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Height at n ≤ 7
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal thm:height-n7 (fourteenth pass); census 275/276/277 plus the diamond; verified against Goddard--Goodwin and GMR2.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The height conjecture holds for every n \le 7 and every prime power q, unconditionally.

Mechanism. The modality theorem: \operatorname {mod}(B : \mathfrak {n}_{n}) = 1 for n = 6, 7. With at most one modulus of B-orbits on the nilradical, the two-moduli case of (*) never arises, so the orbital-variety theorem closes every subvariety. The modality inputs are published rows discharged against machine certificates (Goddard--Goodwin; GMR2).
Uses: The height conjecture, (*): the characteristic-p subvariety inference, Orbital varieties are Lagrangian, Borel modality.

fr:title.text: (M8): the per-cell modality reduction at n = 8

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (M8): the per-cell modality reduction at n = 8
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal thm:m8 (sixteenth pass); pseudo_levi_gap.sage all-pass; commit afdac1f.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: (M8). Every cell of the n = 8 address decomposition has per-cell modality small enough that no cell can carry a violation of (*).

Mechanism. Two ingredients. Pseudo-Levi collapse: the per-cell modality satisfies M(8) = 1, so each cell is a one-modulus problem of the kind height at n \le 7 already handles. Torus-defect dichotomy: a cell either has torus defect placing it below the threshold, or lies in the gap-7 regime where Lang--Weil against 4v^9 excludes it. The two cases are exhaustive.

Status. Proven by theory, conditional only on the published GMR2014 data for A_7 (degree 9, leading coefficient 4). The genericity step in pseudo_levi_gap.sage needs |F| \gtrsim 10^4 to be visible numerically; the argument itself is characteristic-free.
Uses: (*): the characteristic-p subvariety inference, Borel modality, U-modality.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Height at n = 8
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal cor:height-n8 (fifteenth and sixteenth passes); commit afdac1f.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The height conjecture holds for n = 8 and every prime power q, conditional only on the published GMR2014 A_7 row.

Mechanism. The address reduction turns (*) at n = 8 into a per-cell statement, and (M8) discharges every cell. The two-moduli locus is exactly the four O4 ideals, which are Steinberg slices of involutions and therefore safe, characteristic-free.
Uses: The height conjecture, (M8): the per-cell modality reduction at n = 8.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (S): the n = 9 reduction
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal subsec:seventeenth and subsec:eighteenth; census53_cells.log (canonical, 53 addresses degree 10 lc 1 per characteristic), sweep16_rank.log (exact-\mathbb {Q} ranks, 16 nonlinear loci); commit e8c7430.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: (S). At n = 9 the violation locus of (*) is covered by finitely many identified loci, all of which are cold.

Mechanism. Three layers, all machine-checked. Sweep census by involutions: 2620 classes, of which the three f = 3 classes are exactly the three maximizer tableaux (verified) and 51 carry f = 2. Linear layer: 4862 ideals across 5 characteristics, all cold, including exact \mathbb {Q}; a covering theorem makes the finite check exhaustive. Cascade: 53 safe ten-moduli loci, with the boundary probe at layer 1 also cold.

The captured f = 2 case is killed characteristic-free by the cross-term and tangent lemmas, and \operatorname {mod}(B : \mathfrak {n}_{9}) = 3 characteristic-free, so no f = 3 violation is available either. The residual ledger is 72 = 53 + \sum c'_i + m_{\text {unknown}}, closed by (S+).
Uses: (*): the characteristic-p subvariety inference, Borel modality.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (S+): the ledger conjecture
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal subsec:seventeenth (statement), subsec:eighteenth (discharge); the jtype truncation bug found and fixed en route; commit e8c7430.

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
(S+). In the n = 9 ledger 72 = 53 + \sum c'_i + m_{\text {unknown}}, \sum c'_i = 19 \iff m_{\text {unknown}} = 0,
and either side implies (S).

Status. Stated as a conjecture during the seventeenth pass and discharged in the eighteenth: c' = [5, 7, 7], so \sum c'_i = 19 and the unknown count is zero. Kept as its own node because it is the hinge the n = 9 argument turns on, and because a n = 10 analogue is the natural next ledger.
Uses: (S): the n = 9 reduction.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Height at n = 9
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal cor:height-n9 (eighteenth pass); census53_cells.log, sweep16_rank.log; commit e8c7430.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The height conjecture holds for n = 9 and every prime power q, conditional on the published A_7 and A_8 modality rows and on the machine certificates below.

Mechanism. (S) covers the violation locus and (S+) closes its ledger; the three maximizers have \operatorname {lc} = 3 and are safe, so no violation survives. Exact address polynomials come from the GR cell engine.
Uses: The height conjecture, (S): the n = 9 reduction, (S+): the ledger conjecture.

Higman's class count, reached through the same Borel-orbit geometry. The chain from the definition of modality to the leading term of \kappa (U_{n}) is complete except for one inequality, and the degree half of it is a theorem for every n.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The class count kappa(U_n)
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: Higman; Pak--Soffer App.~A for the known values.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: For the unitriangular group U_{n} = U_{n}(\mathbb {F}_q), let \kappa (U_{n}) = \kappa (U_{n}(\mathbb {F}_q)) denote its number of conjugacy classes. Higman's conjecture: \kappa (U_{n}) is polynomial in q for each n.

Where polynomiality is known — n \le 16, Pak--Soffer — write \deg \kappa (U_{n}) and \operatorname {lc} \kappa (U_{n}) for the degree and the leading coefficient. The growth program is the study of these two numbers: the degree law for the degree, the leading-term law for the leading coefficient.
Uses: Setup: conjugation over a finite field.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Borel modality
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal sec:modality; published rows Goddard--Goodwin, GMR 2014.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: For an algebraic group action, modality is the maximum number of parameters of orbits. Write \operatorname {mod}(B : \mathfrak {n}_{n}) for the modality of B = T \ltimes U_{n} acting on its nilradical \mathfrak {n}_{n}, and \operatorname {mod}(Q : V) for the analogous invariant of a parabolic or reductive factor Q acting on a module V.

This is the one invariant both halves of the program share: it bounds \deg \kappa (U_{n}) from above through Theorem D, and it is what the height ladder spends — \operatorname {mod}(B : \mathfrak {n}_{n}) = 1 is exactly why height at n \le 7 goes through and why n = 8 does not.
Uses: Setup: conjugation over a finite field.

For a U-stable irreducible subvariety W \subseteq \mathfrak {n},
\operatorname {umod}(W) = \dim W - \max _{y \in W} \dim U \cdot y,
the dimension of the generic-orbit space; and \operatorname {umod}(w) = \operatorname {umod}(\overline {\text {genStr}(w)}) per sweep stratum.

For a composition c \vdash n with block sizes c_i, write \operatorname {umod}(\mathfrak {n}_{c}) for the U-modality of the parabolic nilradical slice. These parabolic values are the ones with a closed form: (Deg-Opt).
Uses: Setup: conjugation over a finite field, Borel modality.

Theorem D. For every U-stable irreducible W: \operatorname {umod}(W) \le f_B(B \cdot \overline {W}) + (n-1) \le \operatorname {mod}(B : \mathfrak {n}_{n}) + (n-1),
and consequently \deg \kappa (U_{n}) \le (n-1) + \operatorname {mod}(B : \mathfrak {n}_{n}) unconditionally.

Role in the skeleton. This is the bridge. It is what ties the growth program to the same Borel-orbit geometry that carries the height conjecture: the invariant \operatorname {mod}(B : \mathfrak {n}_{n}) bounding Higman's degree is the same one the height ladder spends. Paired with the lower bound of the growth theorem it pins \deg \kappa (U_{n}) from both sides, which is the content of the degree law.
Uses: The class count kappa(U_n), Borel modality, U-modality.

Fix a composition c = (c_1, \dots , c_\ell ) of n and let y \in \mathfrak {n}_{c} be B-generic. Write z_u(c) = \dim (\mathfrak {z}(y) \cap \mathfrak {u}),
the dimension of the centralizer of a generic element inside the upper triangular nilpotent Lie algebra.

For parabolic slices the modality is then \operatorname {umod}(\mathfrak {n}_{c}) = d_c - \frac {n(n - 1)}{2} + z_u(c), \qquad d_c = \sum _i c_i^2 - n,
where d_c adjusts the flag count. So computing \operatorname {umod}(\mathfrak {n}_{c}) is computing z_u(c), which is what the graded count does.
Uses: U-modality.

Here I_s = [i(s), j(s)] are the level intervals of the unimodal level decomposition. This is defined for unimodal c only: non-unimodal c has no density and no such decomposition, which is the reason (P5) is a separate and harder statement from (Deg-Opt).
Uses: z_u(c) and the modality formula.

z_u(c) = \sum _{k \ge 1} N_{k}(c) + e_0(c),
where N_{k}(c) counts the pairs (s, t) with i(s) \le i(t)+k \le j(s) \le j(t)+k, and the defect term is e_0(c) = \dim (\mathfrak {s} \cap \operatorname {Ad}(\bar g) \mathfrak {u}_L) \quad \text {for generic } \bar g \in L.

Consequence. z_u(c) \ge \sum _{k \ge 1} N_{k}(c) unconditionally, i.e. e_0(c) \ge 0. This is the load-bearing exactness statement under (Deg-Opt): the grand formula is the graded count plus a defect that is proven non-negative, not estimated.
Uses: z_u(c) and the modality formula, The thread algebra.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (Deg-Opt): the grand formula for umod
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: scratch_nineteenth.md, grand formula A theorem via H1--H12; machine evidence umod_tables.tsv (11,487 exact rows, n \le 17).

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
(Deg-Opt). For every composition c = (c_1, \dots , c_\ell ) of n: \operatorname {umod}(\mathfrak {n}_{c}) = \frac {1}{2}\bigl [n + \sum _i c_i^2 - \sum \Delta ^2\bigr ] + e_0(c),
where \Delta ranges over all consecutive jumps of the zero-padded profile (0, c_1, \dots , c_\ell , 0), so that \sum \Delta ^2 is the wall penalty and e_0(c) the thread-algebra defect of the graded count.
The formula is exact and unimodal in c. Its three inputs are (P4) (the maximum), (P5) (extension off the unimodal locus) and (P6) (the collapse identity and the period-6 structure).

Uses: z_u(c) and the modality formula, The graded count for z_u (H4), (P4): the maximum of umod over compositions, (P5): the grand formula off the unimodal locus, (P6): the collapse identity and the period-6 structure.

fr:title.text: (P4): the maximum of umod over compositions

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (P4): the maximum of umod over compositions
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: scratch_nineteenth.md Result (P4); certificates mlaw_close.py, o2_symbolic and o2_singular.

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
(P4). \max _{c \vdash n} \operatorname {umod}(\mathfrak {n}_{c}) = \lfloor n(n+6)/12 \rfloor ,
attained exactly by the period-6 maximizer shapes.

Mechanism. Poset-interval induction (H10--H12): the argmax is shown unimodal, so the maximum can be computed on the unimodal locus where (Deg-Opt) is available in closed form, and the period-6 shapes are exhibited as attaining it.

Consequence. With the growth theorem this makes the floor of the degree law unconditional at every n. It is also what makes \lfloor n(n+6)/12 \rfloor the right closed form to look for in the first place.
Uses: z_u(c) and the modality formula, (P6): the collapse identity and the period-6 structure.

fr:title.text: (P5): the grand formula off the unimodal locus

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (P5): the grand formula off the unimodal locus
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: scratch_nineteenth.md Results H15--H17 and the 2026-08-21 finish-off (Theorem O); certificates p5_vtprime, p5_lemmaV_asym.

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
(P5). The grand formula of (Deg-Opt) extends to all compositions: \operatorname {umod}(c) = \text {grand}(\text {core}) + \sum _{\text {dips}} \binom {v+1}{2},
so that the non-unimodal case is the unimodal case plus an explicit dip correction.

Status. Reduced, not closed. The chain is H15--H17: H15 gives the all-compositions formula (exact on 4083 rows, plus certified two-draw z_u() exhaustively at n = 13 and at 14, 15); H16 gives the valley cap v \le M_2(\text {core}) - 1 with packing and abstract optimization, exact and violation-free for 8 \le n \le 40, with the tail closed by Theorem O; H17 is the section trick, reducing the remaining content to Lemma V. The sole residue is multi-block Lemma V, hence (NS).

Warning. The intermediate tool (P5') is refuted from n = 10 — the deep valleys (4,1,5) and (5,1,5) overshoot. That is a failure of the tool, not of (P5); do not cite p5_vt_check's "FAILURES" line, which reports a superseded condition.
Uses: z_u(c) and the modality formula, Lemma V, (NS): the strict/centralizer inequality.

fr:title.text: (P6): the collapse identity and the period-6 structure

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (P6): the collapse identity and the period-6 structure

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
(P6). For unimodal c, e_0(c) = F(c') - F(c),
where c' is the canonical unimodalization — the collapse identity. So the defect term of (Deg-Opt) is itself in closed form on the unimodal locus. Consequently F + e_0 is constant on unimodalization classes and no argmax is spiky.

Mechanism. H7, a copositive inequality whose extremal roots are those of x^2 - x + 1 — which is where the period 6 in n comes from, and hence where \lfloor n(n+6)/12 \rfloor gets its 12. H8 is the peak-shaving step: F + e_0 = F(c') rules out spiky argmaxima, which is what (P4) needs to run its induction.
Uses: z_u(c) and the modality formula, The graded count for z_u (H4).

For every n and every prime power q, \kappa (U_{n}(\mathbb {F}_q)) \ge q^{\lfloor n(n+6)/12 \rfloor } \bigl (1 + O(q^{-1/2})\bigr )
along Frobenius towers in every characteristic. Consequently, where \kappa (U_{n}) is polynomial, \deg \kappa (U_{n}) \ge \lfloor n(n+6)/12 \rfloor ; and combined with Theorem D, \operatorname {mod}(B : \mathfrak {n}_{n}) \ge \lfloor n(n+6)/12 \rfloor - (n-1)
for every n, unconditionally.

Mechanism. Rosenlicht plus Lang on the sweep strata. The generic strata of maximal U-modality each contribute q^{\operatorname {umod}}(1 + O(q^{-1/2})) Frobenius-stable orbits, and disjointness makes the contributions add. The floor is attained by the explicit period-6 maximizer shapes of (P4).
Warning. This re-proves Higman's q^{\lfloor n(n+6)/12 \rfloor } lower bound (Vera-López--Arregi 2003 for small n). Check h2-literature-attribution before claiming new content here.
Uses: The class count kappa(U_n), Theorem D: the modality cap, (Deg-Opt): the grand formula for umod, (P4): the maximum of umod over compositions.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The degree law
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: lc_law.md Theorem C/D; scratch_nineteenth.md for the n \le 17 table.

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
\deg \kappa (U_{n}) = \lfloor n(n+6)/12 \rfloor ,
with equality in the modality cap: \deg \kappa (U_{n}) = (n-1) + \operatorname {mod}(B : \mathfrak {n}_{n}).

Status. The lower bound is a theorem, the growth theorem; the upper bound is Theorem D; what is conjectural is that they meet. Both sides are known for n \le 9. For n = 10 \dots 16 the resulting lower bounds on \operatorname {mod}(B : \mathfrak {n}_{n}) — from 4 up to 14 — are unconditional, using VLA 2003, GMR 2014 and the Pak--Soffer Appendix A degrees. Verified n \le 16; the n = 17 prediction (degree 32) runs ahead of the literature.
Uses: The class count kappa(U_n), Theorem D: the modality cap, The growth theorem.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The leading-term law
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: scratch_nineteenth.md; Pak--Soffer for the published values.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: For n \ge 8: \deg \kappa (U_{n}) = \lfloor n(n+6)/12 \rfloor , \qquad \operatorname {lc} \kappa (U_{n}) = n / \gcd (n, 6).

The unique exception in all data is the n = 7 sport, \operatorname {lc} \kappa (U_{7}) = 8 = 7 + 1: seven maximizers on formula — (2,3,2) is the seventh — plus one extra class from the non-unimodal tie (1,2,1,2,1). Verified against every published value, n \le 16, with twelve straight (\deg , \operatorname {lc}) matches for n = 6 \dots 17.
Status. The unimodal half is a theorem, the M-law. What is missing is the passage from parabolic argmax counts to \operatorname {lc} \kappa (U_{n}), which is (TOP-X).
Uses: The class count kappa(U_n), The degree law, The M-law: the unimodal side of the leading-term law, (TOP-X): rigidity of maximal modality.

fr:title.text: The M-law: the unimodal side of the leading-term law

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The M-law: the unimodal side of the leading-term law

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
the M-law. The argmax count of the grand formula over unimodal compositions satisfies M_{\mathrm {unimodal}}(n) = n / \gcd (n, 6)
exactly, for all n \ge 8.

Mechanism. Three steps, H13--H13''. The sinusoidal move inequality bounds the g-oscillation by 1, with \varepsilon \in \{0,1,2\} and mass (n\rho - \kappa )/6. Then a Diophantine classification of the exact maximizers, c \leftrightarrow (\ell , t, a, \varepsilon ): Lemma A gives \rho \in \{r, r+6\}, Lemma B gives \ell \le 6, Lemma C the exact correspondence, with \ell = 4 isolated by u_{\ell +1} = \pm 1 and \ell = 5 giving families with u_6 = v_6 = 0. Finally the case 6 \mid n closes by sinusoids.
Status. Machine-verified n \le 40 directly, and certified to n \le 911 by mlaw_close.py over 40 stable types.
Uses: (Deg-Opt): the grand formula for umod, (P4): the maximum of umod over compositions, (P6): the collapse identity and the period-6 structure.
(TOP-X). Every U-stable irreducible W with maximal \operatorname {umod}(W) is dense in a maximizer sweep stratum.

Role in the skeleton. This is what carries the M-law across to \operatorname {lc} \kappa (U_{n}): without it, the argmax count over parabolic nilradicals need not be the count of top-dimensional sweep strata, and the leading-term law does not follow. It is the leading-coefficient twin of the rigidity statements the height ladder needs.
Status. Proven for n \le 16 by Corollary F's squeeze — which is also why the leading-term law is verified exactly on the range where published values exist. Open in general.
Uses: U-modality, (P4): the maximum of umod over compositions.
Two live fronts. The (NS) chain is the sole residue of the growth program; the germ-scale front is where the wall program ran out, and is kept on the record because what it refuted is load-bearing.
A split of a composition c = (c_L, v, c_R) isolates a middle block of size v — the longest part, +1 convention — with flanks c_L and c_R.

The split is tall if \max (c_L) \ge v \quad \text {and} \quad \max (c_R) \ge v,
and dominated if moreover c_L[-1] > v and c_R[0] > v. The three classes nest: dominated \subset dip \subset tall.
Write c' for the reductive quotient datum of a split, and \widetilde {L}, \widetilde {R} for the flanks with the v longest parts incremented — the modules the Fredholm ledger is computed in.
Uses: U-modality, z_u(c) and the modality formula.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Lemma V
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: result13_addendum.md; certificates p5_vtprime (EQUALITY), p5_lemmaV_asym; p5_vt_check's "FAILURES" line reports the superseded condition only.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Lemma V, as originally stated: for a split c = (c_L, v, c_R) with reductive quotient data c', z_u(c) \le z_u(c') + v^2.
Status. False as stated over all splits: 958 counterexample splits in umod_tables.tsv at n \le 12. The smallest is c = (1,2,3,1) split as (1) \mid (2) \mid (3,1), where 11 > 6 + 4.

Two regimes survive and are proven. All 3-block splits (a, v, b) — H17', five sub-lemmas: \sigma -avoidance (V-t') giving \dim K \le z' with equality; the decomposition K = x_{XY} \oplus K_0; and a quotient-restriction injection into intertwiners whose kernel is killed by the \binom {v}{2} + \binom {v}{2} against v^2 count, with \text {intw} = \binom {|a-b|}{2}. And the tall regime, Tall-Lemma V.

Warning. The old condition (V-t) fails when |a - b| \ge 2, at \binom {|a-b|}{2}; (V-t') is its repair. (V-t') is itself false in the multi-block setting, and \mathcal {V}_0 \le v^2 holds only for the \mathfrak {k}-version.
Superseded by: Tall-Lemma V for the tall regime; (NS): the strict/centralizer inequality for the general case.
Uses: z_u(c) and the modality formula, Splits, flanks, tallness.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Tall-Lemma V
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: result13_addendum.md 13(f)--(l); ns_theta.log, tall_exact2.py and .log, dip_exact.py and .log. Note tall_exact2, dip_exact and ns_session_state were lost pre-commit and regenerated from umod_tables.tsv, reproducing the cited numbers exactly.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: For every tall split, Lemma V holds with equality.
Status. Zero violations in 11,452 tall splits, against 958 failures all of which are off-tall (tall_exact2.log).

Mechanism. Tallness is exactly the scope, and the three cases say why. Dominated splits carry the gain in the kernel of the fibration map \Theta , where \dim \ker \Theta = v^2; tall-not-dominated carry it in the image; off-tall breaks the balance by exactly +1, an S-mode through \ker \alpha . The Q-fibration machinery of (Q-MOD) consumes precisely tallness and nothing more.
Uses: Splits, flanks, tallness, Lemma V.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (NS): the strict/centralizer inequality
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: scratch_nineteenth.md Result 13, items 15(e)--(f); result13_addendum.md; instruments ns_*.sage, mb_*.sage.

fr:mainmatter.html:p:
(NS). N_{\mathrm {strict}} \le N_z,
where N_{\mathrm {strict}} is the nullity of the pairing on honest strict Hom-triples and N_z the centralizer-side count.

Role in the skeleton. This is the sole residue of the whole chain. By the exact ledger the Fredholm ledger, multi-block Lemma V follows from it; and Lemma V is the last open input to (P5), hence to (Deg-Opt). Everything else in the growth program is proven.
Status. Measured with equality, N_{\mathrm {strict}} = N_z, 13/13 (mb_dual.sage). Two independent reductions exist and neither has closed it: (Q-MOD) and the peeling induction.
Warning. ns_elim_defs.sage as committed is the pre-fix draft. Measure (NS) only through ns_clean.sage or mb_dual.sage until it is repaired.
Uses: Splits, flanks, tallness, Lemma V, The Fredholm ledger.

For a tall split with flanks \widetilde {L}, \widetilde {R}, the ledger is exact: Lemma V holds if and only if N_{\mathrm {weak}} \le N_z + \binom {v+1}{2},
while N_{\mathrm {weak}} \le N_{\mathrm {strict}} + \binom {v+1}{2} is automatic. Hence multi-block Lemma V follows from (NS).

Mechanism. The extension-module theorem: \ker \Phi _c^* is the space of strict \operatorname {Hom}_\Lambda (\widetilde {L}, \widetilde {R})-triples with a \binom {v+1}{2} belowdiagonal relaxation, of dimension \hom (\tilde \lambda , \tilde \mu ) - v^2 + \binom {v+1}{2}. The G-identity gives \dim G = \hom (\tilde \lambda , \tilde \mu ) - \hom (\lambda , \mu ), and \operatorname {codim} R I_c = \operatorname {rank} P by trace duality. The five-equation centralizer system then computes \dim z_q(y) bit-exactly (ns_lift.sage), reducing everything to one rank identity \operatorname {rank}(B, C, D) = \operatorname {rank}(D') + n_L v + v n_R.
Uses: Splits, flanks, tallness, Lemma V, Tall-Lemma V.
(Q-MOD). (NS) is equivalent to \operatorname {mod}(Q : \mathfrak {n}_{c}) \le \operatorname {umod}(c'), \qquad Q = U(L) \times \mathrm {GL}(W) \times U(R) \ltimes N.

Mechanism. Pass to a generic element and split off the reductive factor. The exact Q-equivariant fibration then makes (Q-MOD) equivalent to T_1 + T_2 \le \operatorname {mod}(A : B), where T_1 is a rank-v determinantal modality. A bonus of the repair is z_q() = z_u(), which is what turns the orbit ledger into (NS) in the first place.
Status. Measured: 807 shapes, slack 0. The equivalence is proven; it has not closed (NS).
Warning. The naive LK_s ledger is wrong. The exact coupling is \mathcal {V}_0^{\mathrm {Ext}} - v^2 = LK_z - LK_s.
Uses: U-modality, (NS): the strict/centralizer inequality.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The peeling induction
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: scratch_nineteenth.md item 15(f); instruments mb_fiber, mb_peel, mb_peelpair, mb_s0, mb_i2, mb_q0, mb_grade, mb_k3, mb_s0s.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: (NS) reduces to two one-peel local comparisons: \text {(C1)} \quad \mathrm {ex}_{s} \le \mathrm {ex}_{z}, \qquad \text {(C2)} \quad q_{s} \le q_{z}.

Mechanism. Exact one-peel ladders N(\text {big}) = N(\text {small}) + \mathrm {ex} + q: a zero-e row makes the pairing factor through the restriction B \to B_0, and N(\text {big}) \cap \text {over-}R_0 = W exactly. The excess obeys the automatic cap \mathrm {ex} \le \operatorname {codim} \operatorname {res} B and, precisely, \mathrm {ex} = \operatorname {codim} - \dim ((S\text {-set} + \operatorname {res} B)/\operatorname {res} B),
so (C1) is equivalent to S_0 \subseteq S_0^{s} + \operatorname {res} B. The kernel moves in lockstep, dN_z = dN_w = dN_s, measured at every peel, and the 3-block case of Lemma V is the base.

Status. Both comparisons hold with equality at all 28 measured peels. The saturation shortcut (I1) — \mathrm {ex}_{z} = \operatorname {codim} \operatorname {res} B — holds at flank length 2 but is refuted at length \ge 3 (mb_k3), exactly where S_0 \not \subseteq \operatorname {res} B; the equivalence (I1) \iff S_0 \subseteq \operatorname {res} B does stand. The rigidity calculus gives S_0 = \operatorname {rig}(\Xi _A), tight 20/20 by a tangent argument, with x \cdot \operatorname {soc} R_0 = 0 proven by corner probes; the dual-symmetry and Q_0-cap routes are refuted.
Uses: Lemma V, (NS): the strict/centralizer inequality.
(W). At every nonvacuous component of the Springer-fiber atlas, the derived image of the second-level piece in the symplectic quotient is Lagrangian.
Role in the skeleton. This was the thesis at the infinitesimal scale — the local form of (*), upgrading the coisotropy of Wall 1 to equality.

Status. Refuted, characteristic-free, from n = 6: the derived image is always isotropic, never Lagrangian, so the wall identity cannot hold at component-generic germs. The salvage conjectures went with it — universal (W-iso) and (C2) are dead, and multi-row components are all-Lagrangian for a reason that does not generalize. The twelfth and thirteenth passes closed the wall program.
Consequence. What the program left behind is the stable depth law: caps, balanced runs, and donate-2-to-nearest, verified 30/30. That, not the wall, is the surviving structure at germ scale.
Uses: The thesis: every bound is half an orbit dimension, Wall 1: coisotropy of the cyclic cocycle, The germ apparatus.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (L2): decreasing monomial germs are vacuous
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal passes 8--10 (shift calculus, monomial census); scratch_L2.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: (L2). Decreasing monomial germs are vacuous in every characteristic.

Role in the skeleton. One of the two positive results the germ-scale search produced. Together with the witness principle — a single component-generic germ certifies its whole component — it is what remains standing after (L3) and (W) fell.
Uses: The germ apparatus.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: (L3): the vacuity family
fr:frontmatter.fr:meta: journal passes 8--11; scratch_L3, scratch_sweep, scratch_tenth, scratch_eleventh.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: (L3), in all three of its forms — (L3), (L3'), (L3'') — asserted that the relevant germ components are vacuous.
Status. Refuted. Nonvacuous components exist from n = 4 onward, and the component atlas of the tenth pass exhibits them explicitly at n = 9 and n = 10.

Consequence. Refuting the family is what forced the wall program: with nonvacuous components in hand, the question became what happens at them, which is (W). The eleventh-pass two-generator lattice normal form was the attack route; the depth law for \lambda _2 \ge 3 is still open, and no closed form exists for r \ge 3.
Superseded by: (W): the wall conjecture, and after its refutation, the stable depth law.
Uses: The germ apparatus, (L2): decreasing monomial germs are vacuous.

The notation layer is a node like any other: it is where every symbol in the forest is defined, and it is the only place a macro may be introduced. Read Forest preamble: the notation layer for the index of the seven notation nodes, the mechanics of forester's \def, and the list of glyphs that currently carry two meanings.

Addresses. Statement nodes are ffi-NNNN, assigned in order of minting and never reassigned. Infrastructure — Forest preamble: the notation layer, the seven macros- nodes, this index — keeps readable addresses, because it is named after what it is rather than after a claim that might be restated.

Taxon and tags. The taxon is the grammatical kind: definition, theorem, proposition, lemma, corollary, conjecture, principle, notation, reference. Tags carry area — foundations, symplectic, height, growth, frontier — and status: proven, open, conditional, refuted. A node tagged refuted is still a node; it is on the record because the refutation is a result.

One claim per node. If a node states two things, it is two nodes. This is why the address space is sparse rather than hierarchical: splitting a node mints new addresses and leaves the old one in place, pointing forward.

Dependencies. Every node carries \import{preamble} for notation and nothing else; each mathematical dependency is a link in the \uses{...} line, because forester derives its backlink graph from links and not from imports. Until proof nodes exist, that line carries what a proof's inline citations would. ./check-dag.py verifies that every link resolves, that the graph is acyclic, and that nothing is stranded.

Provenance. Every statement node records where it came from — the journal section, the experiment record, the paper — as frontmatter \meta{provenance}{...}. It is metadata rather than prose: provenance is a fact about the node, not part of what the node claims, so the page does not print it. The concordance ADDRESSES.md lists it in full. Proofs live in the journal; proof nodes are a later pass.
